BIOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #19
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: BIOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Evolution? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Evolution.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Evolution.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Evolution.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Evolution.

2. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. joule (J)
   C. newton (N)
   D. pascal (Pa)

3. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 37 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 100 °C

4. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

5. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Iron rusting

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Response and Coordination 2.2 Support and Movement 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Response and Coordination 2.2 Support and Movement 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Response and Coordination 2.2 Support and Movement 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Response and Coordination 2.2 Support and Movement 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Response and Coordination 2.2 Support and Movement 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of.

7. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Support and Movement 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Animals 3.1 Response and Coor? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Support and Movement 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Animals 3.1 Response and Coor.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Support and Movement 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Animals 3.1 Response and Coor.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Support and Movement 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Animals 3.1 Response and Coor.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Support and Movement 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Animals 3.1 Response and Coor.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Support and Movement in Animals? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Support and Movement in Animals.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Support and Movement in Animals.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Support and Movement in Animals.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Support and Movement in Animals.

10. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only carbon dioxide

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Genetics? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Genetics.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Genetics.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Genetics.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Genetics.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Response and Coordination in Plants? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Response and Coordination in Plants.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Response and Coordination in Plants.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Response and Coordination in Plants.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Response and Coordination in Plants.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
